experience-00-overview-fig1.title: Two front doors, one product
experience-00-overview-fig1.takeaway: Web and MCP share authorization and authoritative state; events flow back to clients.

nodes.title: Human operator
nodes.subtitle: Inspect and decide
nodes.detail:
Choose the interface,
not a different product.

nodes.title: Web UI
nodes.subtitle: Project and run views
nodes.detail:
Opens the watch request;
receives API event payloads.

nodes.title: MCP client
nodes.subtitle: Assistant tool caller
nodes.detail:
Makes explicit tool calls;
surfaces decisions to people.

nodes.title: Product state
nodes.subtitle: Projects, teams, runs
nodes.detail:
API-authorized reads and
mutations; no MCP bypass.

nodes.title: Agentweaver API
nodes.subtitle: Authorization boundary
nodes.detail:
Owns resource checks and
access to product state.

nodes.title: MCP server
nodes.subtitle: Authenticated adapter
nodes.detail:
Forwards the exact caller
token to the API.

experience-00-overview-fig1.note: Browser opens the connection; API sends event payloads. MCP results return through MCP.

experience-mcp-client-fig1.title: Assistant-driven work
experience-mcp-client-fig1.takeaway: Choose one intake path, inspect the result, and preserve explicit human decisions.

nodes.title: Human + assistant
nodes.subtitle: Agree on the work
nodes.detail:
The assistant explains actions;
a person supplies judgment.

nodes.title: Project and team
nodes.subtitle: Inspect or create
nodes.detail:
Named roles and charters
belong to the project.

nodes.title: Choose intake
nodes.subtitle: Queue OR start now
nodes.detail:
Ready pickup is an alternative
to an immediate start.

nodes.title: Human review
nodes.subtitle: Read before deciding
nodes.detail:
MCP approve/decline is binary.
Feedback uses other surfaces.

nodes.title: State and artifacts
nodes.subtitle: Watch, list, read
nodes.detail:
Progress and results return
through the MCP adapter.

nodes.title: Coordinator
nodes.subtitle: Runs and child work
nodes.detail:
Queued: claim then unattended.
Direct: no outcome gate.

experience-mcp-client-fig1.note: Define Outcome is the third start variant: draft, obtain authorized confirmation, then dispatch.

experience-onboarding-auth-fig1.title: Browser sign-in and readiness
experience-onboarding-auth-fig1.takeaway: Entra establishes identity; AI readiness and optional GitHub capabilities remain separate.

nodes.title: Browser
nodes.subtitle: Start Entra sign-in
nodes.detail:
The API binds this request
to expiring browser state.

nodes.title: Auth API
nodes.subtitle: Save state and PKCE
nodes.detail:
The verifier stays server-side.
Redirect carries a challenge.

nodes.title: Microsoft Entra
nodes.subtitle: Authenticate identity
nodes.detail:
Not GitHub login;
not repository authorization.

nodes.title: Ready app shell
nodes.subtitle: Continue when ready
nodes.detail:
GitHub Repo App access is
optional for GitHub work.

nodes.title: Browser session
nodes.subtitle: One-time code exchange
nodes.detail:
Frontend exchanges a code;
no raw token in callback URL.

nodes.title: Callback checks
nodes.subtitle: Consume state once
nodes.detail:
Validate Entra response and
bound browser callback.

experience-onboarding-auth-fig1.note: Session identity does not grant repository access, provider readiness, or project membership.

experience-onboarding-auth-fig2.title: MCP uses broker credentials
experience-onboarding-auth-fig2.takeaway: An Entra-backed consent flow issues the exact-resource credential accepted by MCP.

nodes.title: MCP client
nodes.subtitle: Discover resource/issuer
nodes.detail:
Use the advertised resource
and authorization server.

nodes.title: Browser consent
nodes.subtitle: Entra-backed session
nodes.detail:
Show client and requested
access; Allow or Deny.

nodes.title: OpenIddict
nodes.subtitle: Bind grant and code
nodes.detail:
Existing consent may skip a
prompt; denial is not success.

nodes.title: Authorized API
nodes.subtitle: Enforce resource access
nodes.detail:
MCP forwards the validated
bearer; API checks again.

nodes.title: MCP boundary
nodes.subtitle: Validate broker token
nodes.detail:
Exact single audience,
subject and mcp:invoke.

nodes.title: Token exchange
nodes.subtitle: Code + verifier
nodes.detail:
Returns Agentweaver token;
not raw Entra or GitHub.

experience-onboarding-auth-fig2.note: Invalid/missing token: 401. Missing scope: 403. No API-key or raw Entra/GitHub fallback.

experience-team-casting-memory-fig1.title: Named teams, governed memory
experience-team-casting-memory-fig1.takeaway: Only eligible database records feed future context; exports are inspectable mirrors.

nodes.title: Cast proposal
nodes.subtitle: Roles, names, charters
nodes.detail:
Inspect the proposal;
confirm the intended change.

nodes.title: Named team
nodes.subtitle: Persist roster and work
nodes.detail:
Agents accumulate records;
records are not auto-policy.

nodes.title: Review knowledge
nodes.subtitle: Memory and decision inbox
nodes.detail:
Authorized promotion;
rejection remains auditable.

nodes.title: Future context
nodes.subtitle: Untrusted structured data
nodes.detail:
Cross-agent memory requires
approved high-value learning.

nodes.title: Eligibility
nodes.subtitle: Filter and budget
nodes.detail:
Active approved boundaries;
cross-team learning/pattern.

nodes.title: Knowledge DB
nodes.subtitle: Authoritative records
nodes.detail:
Exported files are mirrors,
not the compiler authority.

experience-team-casting-memory-fig1.note: A cross-team tag alone is insufficient. Approved + high importance + learning/pattern are required.

canonical-a2a-execution.title: Remote leaves, worker-owned graph
canonical-a2a-execution.takeaway: A2A moves leaf turns into sandbox pods, not orchestration or durable state ownership.

nodes.title: Workflow graph
nodes.subtitle: Orchestration and gates
nodes.detail:
Graph progression and human
gates stay worker-side.

nodes.title: RemoteAgentProxy
nodes.subtitle: Leaf-turn adapter
nodes.detail:
Configure run context;
forward the leaf invocation.

nodes.title: Event recorder
nodes.subtitle: Decode returned events
nodes.detail:
Records pod event data parts;
no direct pod-to-UI stream.

nodes.title: Sandbox pod
nodes.subtitle: AgentHost + executor
nodes.detail:
No database/checkpoint-store
access from AgentHost.

nodes.title: Durable state
nodes.subtitle: Checkpoints and events
nodes.detail:
Worker persists progress;
API reads event cursors.

nodes.title: Web timeline
nodes.subtitle: API stream consumer
nodes.detail:
Shows persisted run events;
not transport-level replay.

canonical-a2a-execution.note: Worker checkpoints and review gates remain authoritative. TLS settings depend on deployment overlay.

experience-a2a-distributed-agents-fig2.title: Remote turns: pause is not failure
experience-a2a-distributed-agents-fig2.takeaway: Claim/configure, observe terminal evidence, and make recovery an explicit policy decision.

nodes.title: Claim a sandbox
nodes.subtitle: Controller/Kubernetes bind
nodes.detail:
Acquire a run-bound pod;
not a pod for each token.

nodes.title: Configure + stream
nodes.subtitle: Inject run context
nodes.detail:
Leaf output returns through
the worker event recorder.

nodes.title: Terminal evidence
nodes.subtitle: agent.turn.end
nodes.detail:
A clean EOF without the
terminal marker is not success.

nodes.title: Checkpoint wait
nodes.subtitle: Human / external gate
nodes.detail:
Active previews or assembly
may retain pod resources.

nodes.title: Visible failure
nodes.subtitle: Incomplete / transport
nodes.detail:
Prior deltas can be preserved;
no seamless replay promise.

nodes.title: Recovery decision
nodes.subtitle: Inspect state and budget
nodes.detail:
Fresh dispatch is deliberate;
side effects may need review.

experience-a2a-distributed-agents-fig2.note: The checkpoint lane is a separate workflow wait, not an automatic recovery path for a failed turn.

experience-operations-fig1.title: Choose the right operations surface
experience-operations-fig1.takeaway: Inspection and configuration have different scopes; MCP parity is intentionally partial.

nodes.title: Diagnostics
nodes.subtitle: Health and checks
nodes.detail:
Inspect explicit failures and
unknown timed-out checks.

nodes.title: Heartbeat + Flow
nodes.subtitle: Pickup and orchestration
nodes.detail:
Automation reports pickup;
Flow shows ongoing work.

nodes.title: Cluster + traces
nodes.subtitle: Capacity and observability
nodes.detail:
No dedicated Cluster or
Observability MCP tools.

nodes.title: Account settings
nodes.subtitle: Authentication / AI access
nodes.detail:
Not a repository-path
sandbox-policy editor.

nodes.title: Platform settings
nodes.subtitle: Model provider controls
nodes.detail:
Global provider configuration
requires admin authority.

nodes.title: Project settings
nodes.subtitle: Repository / sandbox
nodes.detail:
Preview approval and lifetime;
MCP setter is narrower.

experience-operations-fig1.note: All surfaces use authorized API operations. sandbox_policy_set changes repository shell_enabled only.

experience-sandbox-pod-execution-fig3.title: A durable run can outlive its pod
experience-sandbox-pod-execution-fig3.takeaway: A review wait may release compute; preview and assembly retention are explicit exceptions.

nodes.title: Active leaf
nodes.subtitle: AgentHost returns output
nodes.detail:
Worker records events and
owns workflow progression.

nodes.title: Worker gate
nodes.subtitle: Human decision requested
nodes.detail:
Persist resumable state;
pause watchdog accounting.

nodes.title: Release decision
nodes.subtitle: Policy and lifecycle checks
nodes.detail:
Release requires support and
no active retention exception.

nodes.title: Resumed work
nodes.subtitle: Continue from saved state
nodes.detail:
A released pod may be replaced;
its name can change.

nodes.title: Durable checkpoint
nodes.subtitle: Session and workspace
nodes.detail:
Load resumable state;
claim/configure if released.

nodes.title: Release or retain
nodes.subtitle: Claim deletion / keep pod
nodes.detail:
Active preview defers deletion;
release failures are logged.

experience-sandbox-pod-execution-fig3.note: Human waiting does not imply zero retained compute. This is not arbitrary failed-turn rehydration.

experience-scaling-operations-fig1.title: Scale roles, keep state shared
experience-scaling-operations-fig1.takeaway: Web serves requests; workers execute; Postgres coordinates durable state; pods run leaves.

nodes.title: Browser
nodes.subtitle: REST and watch client
nodes.detail:
Connects to web replicas;
not a worker-local queue.

nodes.title: Web tier
nodes.subtitle: Requests and event reads
nodes.detail:
Uses shared durable state;
reads event cursors.

nodes.title: Worker tier
nodes.subtitle: Execution and ownership
nodes.detail:
CPU 70% / memory 80%;
leases and workflow state.

nodes.title: Current boundary
nodes.subtitle: Configuration, not a probe
nodes.detail:
Checked-in scaling settings
are not live cluster evidence.

nodes.title: Postgres
nodes.subtitle: Shared durable state
nodes.detail:
Event relay polls the table;
not LISTEN/NOTIFY.

nodes.title: Sandbox pods
nodes.subtitle: Remote AgentHost leaves
nodes.detail:
Return events to the worker;
no direct pod DB access.

experience-scaling-operations-fig1.note: Worker HPA is active; KEDA and web HPA blocks are commented proposals. Kubernetes owns scheduling.

experience-scaling-operations-fig3.title: Lease transfer is not turn replay
experience-scaling-operations-fig3.takeaway: An expired owner can be replaced; continuation depends on the persisted run state.

nodes.title: Worker A
nodes.subtitle: Guarded lease claim
nodes.detail:
Renewals must match both
owner and fencing token.

nodes.title: Lease expires
nodes.subtitle: Renewals cease
nodes.detail:
Failure is not a message;
expiry permits a later claim.

nodes.title: Worker B
nodes.subtitle: Win eligible next claim
nodes.detail:
Old-token terminal ownership
checks reject stale results.

nodes.title: Visible failure
nodes.subtitle: Stranded child / root
nodes.detail:
Child may be redispatched;
no automatic mid-turn replay.

nodes.title: Inspect run state
nodes.subtitle: Checkpoint or work plan
nodes.detail:
AwaitingReview, coordinator,
and stranded turns differ.

nodes.title: Durable recovery
nodes.subtitle: Eligible saved state
nodes.detail:
Recover only supported state;
missing checkpoints surface.

experience-scaling-operations-fig3.note: Fencing protects guarded ownership operations, not every external tool side effect.

experience-review-workspace-merge-fig1.title: Inspect, decide, then integrate
experience-review-workspace-merge-fig1.takeaway: Approval identifies a candidate; guarded local merge can also include target-side changes.

nodes.title: Run candidate
nodes.subtitle: Worktree + recorded hash
nodes.detail:
Inspect the actual candidate
before submitting a decision.

nodes.title: Review decision
nodes.subtitle: Authorized run reviewer
nodes.detail:
MCP run_review is binary;
web supports feedback.

nodes.title: Guarded merge
nodes.subtitle: Lock, CAS, hash check
nodes.detail:
Changed candidate fails checks;
conflicts are visible.

nodes.title: Revised candidate
nodes.subtitle: Feedback drives revision
nodes.detail:
A new candidate needs review;
no automatic approval.

nodes.title: Declined / blocked
nodes.subtitle: No successful integration
nodes.detail:
Decline, busy repository and
merge conflict are distinct.

nodes.title: Merged history
nodes.subtitle: Local destination updated
nodes.detail:
Final tree may include newer
target and special Squad state.

experience-review-workspace-merge-fig1.note: Request changes produces the revised-candidate lane. Conflicts/busy/hash mismatch never imply merged.

experience-review-workspace-merge-fig2.title: Browse a ref without changing it
experience-review-workspace-merge-fig2.takeaway: Select an allowed ref, inspect its tree, and read content through read-only operations.

nodes.title: Workspace reader
nodes.subtitle: Web page or MCP client
nodes.detail:
Browsing does not check out,
edit, approve or merge.

nodes.title: Available refs
nodes.subtitle: Base, run, assembly
nodes.detail:
Only available allowed refs;
default is the base branch.

nodes.title: Selected ref
nodes.subtitle: Explicit browsing context
nodes.detail:
Changing ref clears the
previous file selection.

nodes.title: Read-only content
nodes.subtitle: Source / Markdown preview
nodes.detail:
Render supported content;
surface truthful limitations.

nodes.title: Selected path
nodes.subtitle: Relative file name
nodes.detail:
Pass both path and ref;
invalid paths are rejected.

nodes.title: File tree
nodes.subtitle: Paths at the selected ref
nodes.detail:
Choose a listed file;
no working-tree mutation.

experience-review-workspace-merge-fig2.note: Unknown refs/files can return 404; invalid paths return 400. Ref browsing is not content approval.

experience-workflows-backlog-fig3.title: One won claim, one reserved run
experience-workflows-backlog-fig3.takeaway: Ready pickup commits claim and reservation before activation; other outcomes do not launch.

nodes.title: Ranked Ready tasks
nodes.subtitle: Heartbeat candidates
nodes.detail:
Top-N limits candidates per
tick, not total concurrency.

nodes.title: Atomic transaction
nodes.subtitle: Claim + run + policy
nodes.detail:
Commit all together;
no orphan losing run.

nodes.title: Activate winner
nodes.subtitle: Use reserved run ID
nodes.detail:
Schedule unattended confirm
attributed to CapturedBy.

nodes.title: Lost / unavailable
nodes.subtitle: No launch by this pickup
nodes.detail:
A winner may own a lost claim;
unavailable leaves Ready.

nodes.title: Claimed failed run
nodes.subtitle: Visible failure reason
nodes.detail:
Do not silently requeue.
Terminalization may log failure.

nodes.title: Coordinator work
nodes.subtitle: Unattended execution
nodes.detail:
No second manual start for
the same captured goal.

experience-workflows-backlog-fig3.note: A won preflight-failure reservation also stays Claimed/Failed. Claim-once is not tool-execution-once.
